parameters.text: There are women who never had the chance to sit in a classroom, hold a textbook, or write their names on a school board.
Yet, somehow, they understood the transcendent power of education better than anyone.
They woke up before the sun, worked with tired hands, and carried dreams that were bigger than their own lives.
Every sacrifice was quiet. Every burden was carried without a single word of regret.
They watched the school gates from the outside, but vowed their children would walk through them.
They might not have known the answers to our homework...
...but they always knew one thing: we had to keep learning.
With every cup of tea, with every quiet whisper to stay awake, they gave us wings.
Today, we are living the dreams they never had the opportunity to pursue.
Every page we read, every door we open carries a little piece of their sacrifice.
They may never have called themselves teachers. But they were our first teachers.
And their wisdom will live through generations.
